what: The heuristic precomputes customer visited/location facts, identifies the unique non-customer depot, and reconstructs directed routing costs from grounded `visit` and `return-to-depot` operator metric costs. At evaluation it finds the current location and unvisited customers, computes an undirected MST connectivity estimate, and constructs a directed nearest-neighbour completion ending at the depot. The final routing estimate blends 25% MST cost with 75% nearest-neighbour route cost. If exact non-derived `capacity()`, `demand(customer)`, and `load()` PNEs are available, it also estimates the number of capacity-forced depot transitions and adds the cheapest corresponding route-break detours. Missing optional resource PNEs simply disable that term.
why: CVRP states primarily differ by current location, visited set, accumulated load, and vehicle-route boundaries. The representative instances have metric-like clustered distance matrices, so an MST captures global cluster connectivity while a nearest-neighbour completion provides stronger ordering sensitivity and a realistic remaining route magnitude. Blending them reduces the instability of a purely greedy tour while retaining guidance that distinguishes customer permutations. Capacity can force expensive depot resets, so an aggregate-demand break term is useful when exact resource PNEs survive translation; routing remains fully operational when they are folded into derived expressions.
